purpose: Teach: しっとり/金色/蒸し/きらきら/ジャージ/ピート/凍っ/膳

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃のお菓子、しっとりした和菓子が懐かしい。
lines.en: I miss those moist wagashi we had when we were young.
lines.style: Slow, distant gaze inward. Warm breath on the opening. Tender melancholy—not regret, but the particular ache of remembering small, good things. Trailing softly at the end.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん。結婚式の金色の屏風、覚えてる?
lines.en: Yes. Do you remember the gold screen at our wedding?
lines.style: Gentle prompt, checking if he remembers too. Voice lifts slightly with affection. A little conspiratorial—sharing the memory. Soft landing on the question.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 蒸し風呂、温泉宿で何度も行ったな。
lines.en: The steam baths at those onsen inns... we went so many times.
lines.style: Eyes closed feeling. Quiet, steady pace. The weight of years in the voice but not heaviness—more like settling. Slight trailing-off, letting the image linger.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃の眼、きらきらしてたわね、お互い。
lines.en: Your eyes were so bright back then. Both of us.
lines.style: Tender observation, almost to herself. Reaches across the table with her voice, not her hands. Slight wonder in it—that brightness is still visible to her now, even if only in memory.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 孫のジャージ、洗濯してあげようかな。
lines.en: Should I wash our grandson's jersey for him?
lines.style: Practical question wrapped in care. Lighter tone—a small thing he can do. Not asking permission, more thinking aloud with purpose. Gentle but present.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お土産のピート風味のお酒、お父さん、お気に入りだった。
lines.en: That peat-flavored liquor you brought back—your father loved it.
lines.style: Soft recollection. Voice drifts into the memory of his father. Warm and wistful without sadness—more like honoring a good taste he had. Trails gently.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 川の水、冬は凍って、子供の頃、滑ったな。
lines.en: The river froze solid in winter when we were kids. We used to slide on it.
lines.style: A child's delight still lives in the memory. Pace picks up slightly—the excitement is still there, caught in amber. Clear, awake voice. Settling back down at the end.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お膳、おもてなしに、よく出したわね。
lines.en: We used to bring out that tray whenever we had guests.
lines.style: Pride and affection braided together. Voice softens at 「おもてなし」—hospitality mattered to her. Closing warmth, like a door shutting gently on something well done.
